findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but after this change no zero-argument method with that name exists anywhere in the class hierarchy: UsernamePasswordForm (the only superclass that defines anything similar) only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at line 160, and neither AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor AbstractFormAuthenticator provides a no-arg version. The services module therefore fails to compile. Either a no-arg overload must be added to UsernamePasswordForm, or the call must be changed to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: Requiring an identified user drops WebAuthn conditional-UI setup on the initial login page
findings.body: In authenticate() (line 115) and challenge(context, error, field) (line 137), the WebAuthn setup is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which (lines 160-162) additionally requires user != null. On a normal initial login no user is set yet, so webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked: the login page never receives the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID or enableWebAuthnConditionalUI attributes, the hidden form //form[@id='webauth'] is not rendered, and passkey autofill / automatic discoverable-key login cannot work. The base code this PR removes explicitly set up the webauthn data "when the user is not already selected". The PR's own tests contradict the new behavior: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication assert the webauthn form and the 'username webauthn' autocomplete on the initial page before any user is identified, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts the same after a failed username, and the webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey tests expect the user to be logged in automatically straight from oauth.openLoginForm(). The fill must also happen when context.getUser() == null (i.e. the condition must not require an identified user), otherwise passkey login on the standard first login page is broken.

findings.title: Broad catch (Exception) can make the 'no webauthn button' check pass spuriously
findings.body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (and the identical block around line 312), the absence of the webauthn form is verified with: try { assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee) { }. Two problems: (1) driver.findElement never returns null, so assertThat(..., nullValue()) can never succeed and the fail() line is dead code; (2) catching Exception rather than NoSuchElementException means any unrelated driver/page error (timeout, stale element, page not loaded) is silently swallowed and the test passes without actually verifying the webauthn form is absent. If the webauthn form is present the AssertionError correctly propagates, but the check should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as done in the other test classes to avoid false passes.
